before:
Glenlaggan Bothy Association — Fabric Repairs Report, Season Ending March

Three shelters were surveyed after the thaw and all three carry outstanding work beyond the year's allowance. The committee's standing practice for a short purse is unchanged: roof and chimney work is undertaken ahead of window replacement, and window replacement ahead of interior lining. Nothing has been struck from the schedule of permitted works, and the warden retains discretion to bring forward any item that has become a hazard to occupants. Volunteers are reminded that lime mortar cannot be worked below four degrees, so the northern shelter's pointing will wait for June regardless of how the money falls. A revised estimate follows in the appendix.

before:
Saltmarsh Tide Gauge — Recording Settings Sheet

The gauge writes a reading every six minutes to the local card and mirrors it to the office once nightly. Under the settings agreed at commissioning, station operators may alter the sampling interval during storm watches, provided the change is noted on the sheet in the hut. Card capacity is sufficient for eleven weeks at the standing interval. The clock is disciplined against the long-wave signal each midnight and drifts less than a second a week in ordinary conditions. Where the mirror fails, the office copy is rebuilt from the card at the next visit, and no reading has been lost by this route since the gauge was installed.
after:
Saltmarsh Tide Gauge — Recording Settings Sheet

The gauge writes a reading every six minutes to the local card and mirrors it to the office once nightly. Under the settings agreed at commissioning, station operators must not alter the sampling interval during storm watches, even where the change would be noted on the sheet in the hut. Card capacity is sufficient for eleven weeks at the standing interval. The clock is disciplined against the long-wave signal each midnight and drifts less than a second a week in ordinary conditions. Where the mirror fails, the office copy is rebuilt from the card at the next visit, and no reading has been lost by this route since the gauge was installed.
variation_site: The altered wording lies in the second sentence.
author_note: Turns a permission into a prohibition with no claim about the world changed.

before:
Cullen Road Allotments — Water Butt Changeover Procedure

The changeover runs on the last Saturday of October and takes about two hours with four hands. Butts are drained to the standpipe channel, lids and downpipe collars are lifted off and stacked by plot number, and the taps are wrapped against frost. Would members kindly make sure that their butt is empty before the crew reaches their plot, as a full butt cannot be tipped safely by two people. The site secretary walks the rows from the top gate and marks off each plot on the clipboard sheet as it is cleared. Anything found broken is set aside by the shed for the spring order.

before:
Kestrel Lane Depot — Standby Pump, Operating Manual, Section 5

The standby set is a diesel-driven centrifugal pump housed in the end bay and coupled to the flood main by a flanged spool. It delivers 41 litres a minute at full head with a clean strainer. Priming is by hand lever at the pump body; the set will not draw on its own from dry. Fuel is drawn from the day tank, which holds enough for a long night's running. The set is exercised on the first working day of each month for a quarter of an hour and the hour meter is read afterwards. Any smoke on load is reported to the depot foreman.

before:
Sandwath Subscription Library — Handling Sheet for Donated Volumes

Donated volumes reach the workroom in crates from the front desk. Each volume is stamped at the title page, then measured across the boards, then sleeved in clear jacket film and shelved on the holding run. The stamp must be the small oval, not the accession oval, and the film must be the acid-free stock held in the cupboard. Measurements go on the slip in millimetres so that the shelving run can be planned before the volumes are moved. Volumes found with loose plates are set aside for the binder and are not sleeved. The crate is signed off by whoever empties it and returned to the desk the same afternoon.

before:
Cranmouth Harbour Office — Notice to Berth Holders, Winter Season

Berth holders are reminded that winter dues fall due on the first of November and that the office is open on weekday mornings for payment. For the coming season, each vessel's dues are worked out by the wetted-area method, from the figures held on the berth card. Where a card is out of date, the office will measure the vessel afloat before the invoice is raised. Dues remain payable whether or not the vessel is lifted out during the season, and unpaid dues after the first of January carry the usual surcharge. Berth holders wishing to query a figure should write to the harbour clerk within fourteen days of receiving the invoice.

before:
Tarn Head Weather Volunteers — Observers' Handbook, Return of Readings

Observers send the daily return by e-mail before nine in the morning, as a plain text attachment with one line per reading. Within each line the fields are separated by semicolons, in the order station code, date, hour, dry bulb, wet bulb, rainfall, remarks. The remarks field may be left empty but the separators before it must still be present. Rainfall is given in millimetres to one decimal and a trace is written as the letter T. Returns that the reading machine cannot take are held for the coordinator, who telephones the observer the same day. Paper returns are still accepted from the two upland stations without a telephone line.

before:
Ravensholt Depot — Turnaround Log, Front Sheet Note

For every entry in this book, a working day means any day on which the depot gates are opened, Saturdays included. Turnaround figures on the following pages are counted in working days from the hour of arrival to the hour the load leaves the yard. The overdue column is filled by the gateman at close of business and the running total is carried to the foot of each page. Where a load is held for inspection, the days of the hold are counted in full and the reason is written in the margin. The monthly summary is copied to the traffic office on the first Monday and the book stays in the gate hut.

before:
Wold Edge Seed Bank — Lending Arrangements for Member Growers

Member growers may draw up to six packets a season from the lending shelf against their card, and are asked to grow out at least one line to seed. Surplus seed from a grown-out line may be passed on to another grower without reference to the bank. Returns are weighed at the counter and entered against the member's card the same day. Lines under quarantine are not lent at all and are marked with a red dot on the shelf label. Members who fail to return a grown-out line for two seasons running are stood down from lending until the committee has considered the matter at its next sitting.
